plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: Nodding, bell-shaped white blossoms with delicate green-tipped inner petals push up through frost, and sometimes snow, on slender stems. Whole woodland floors in the UK and Europe turn white with them.
plants.bloomingSeason: January to February, in late winter
plants.location: Woodlands and gardens across the United Kingdom and Europe
plants.funFact: Snowdrops make natural antifreeze-like compounds in their tissues. This helps them flower in cold that would stop most plants. Their bulbs are also the original source of galantamine, a compound used in medicine.

plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: Bare branches burst into fragrant blossoms in white, blush and deep pink while winter still holds the landscape. The scent is sweet and spicy, and it carries on cold air.
plants.bloomingSeason: January to February, ahead of cherry blossom season
plants.location: Japan and the Yangtze River region of China, in parks, shrines and orchards
plants.funFact: Ume blooms weeks before cherry trees. In Japan and China it is a symbol of perseverance and the coming spring, and its sour fruit is pickled into umeboshi.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs carry large, rose-like flowers, often double and up to about five inches across, in shades from pure white to deep crimson. Against the dark green leaves they look especially bright in late winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring, February to April
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea and China, and widely grown in mild-winter gardens such as the southeastern United States
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a close cousin of Camellia sinensis, the plant that gives us tea. Gardeners have bred thousands of cultivars of the ornamental species.

plants.name: Agapanthus africanus
plants.description: Rounded clusters of deep blue, trumpet-shaped flowers rise on tall, slender stalks above strappy leaves. In the southern summer they give color to coastal gardens and fynbos slopes.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer, December to February, in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Agapanthus is often called the 'Lily of the Nile', but it is neither a true lily nor from the Nile. Its name comes from Greek words meaning 'love flower'.
